subject: Aurora-Lite elevated 5xx/timeouts — stabilization update & remediation plan
messages:
From: Ian Holden <ian.holden@skylabs.com>
To: aisha.rahman@redwood.ai, support@redwood.ai
Cc: sre@skylabs.com
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Elevated 5xx + timeouts from aurora-lite model since 07:50 PT

Hi Aisha / Redwood team,

We started seeing a spike of 5xx responses and request timeouts against the aurora-lite model (model id: aurora-lite-v2.3) in our production traffic at ~07:50 PT. Impact: ~18% of generation requests failing with 500 / 504 over the last 30 mins, affecting our assistant product.

Quick details:
- Sample request ids attached in skylabs-logs-09-12.tar.gz.
- Failures correlate with longer contexts (>=2k tokens) but we also see some short-context 5xx bursts.
- No recent changes on our side; traffic profile steady.

Can you confirm whether this is a known degradation and estimated ETA for stabilization? We’re prepared to route traffic to a fallback model if that helps.

Thanks,
Ian
Ian Holden
SRE Lead, SkyLabs

Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Elevated 5xx + timeouts from aurora-lite model since 07:50 PT

Ian — thanks for the heads up. We’ve opened an incident bridge and the infra team is triaging now (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-11234).

Immediate actions we’ve taken:
- Scoped traffic: routing rule applied to divert 25% of SkyLabs traffic to aurora-stable-2.1 as a safety fallback.
- Disabled the latest quantized kernel variant for aurora-lite-v2.3 on affected pools.
- Collected logs and trace ids (we received your attachment).

We’ll post a stabilization update in 30 minutes or sooner. I’ve looped in Ben (ops lead), Priyom (model infra), and Monica (CS) to coordinate next steps and customer comms.

Apologies for the disruption — we’re on it.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: aisha.rahman@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai, monica.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 08:36:00 -07:00
Subject: [Internal] Triage notes: aurora-lite-v2.3 5xx spike

Team — quick triage notes from the bridge:

Observations:
- Kernel crashes observed on a subset of GPU hosts (NVIDIA driver combo 535.54 + quantized op path). Crash signature points to KV-cache eviction race when sequence lengths cross a particular boundary (~2048 steps).
- Queue growth starts ~07:49; by 07:55 the autoscaler ramped but pods using quantized kernel failed to process, leading to client 504s.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Disabled quantized kernel variant (rolled to fp16 kernel) for the affected GPU pool (completed 08:28).
- Increased burst capacity for dedicated pools serving SkyLabs.
- Rollback flag prepared for aurora-lite to previous non-quantized baseline if instability persists.

Action items:
- Priyom: patch to KV-cache eviction selector to avoid race — target hotfix v2.3.1 today. Attach: aurora-lite-2.3-kernel-diff.patch
- Monica/CS: confirm SKUs and credit policy with Contracts if prolonged impact (>4h).
- Aisha: send customer stabilization update and ETA.

Ben
Senior Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
From: aisha.rahman@redwood.ai <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Ian Holden <ian.holden@skylabs.com>, SkyLabs SRE <sre@skylabs.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Update: aurora-lite-v2.3 — interim stabilization and next steps

Ian — quick update from the bridge.

What we changed so far (completed):
- Disabled quantized kernel path for aurora-lite-v2.3 on affected pools (moved requests to fp16 execution).
- Diverted 25% of your traffic to aurora-stable-2.1 to reduce user-visible failures while we stabilize v2.3.
- Increased burst capacity by +30% on dedicated hosts serving your account.

Observed result: error rate dropped from ~18% to ~2% in the 20 minutes after mitigations. We’re continuing to monitor.

Planned next steps (today):
- Engineering will deploy a hotfix to the KV-cache eviction code (Priyom) and run canary tests (target: 13:30 PT).
- If canary passes, we’ll gradually re-enable a constrained quantized kernel on a small subset of canary hosts and measure error rate / latency.
- We expect full re-enablement or safe rollback decision within 6 hours.

Attachments: service-bridge-notes-20260912.pdf (bridge notes, timeline), skylabs-logs-09-12.tar.gz (your logs we correlated).

If you’d prefer we keep all traffic on aurora-stable-2.1 until the patch is validated, tell us now and we’ll extend the diversion window.

We’ll post another update as soon as the hotfix is validated or after the canary window. Apologies again for the disruption and thanks for the quick reporting — it helped narrow the vector.

Regards,
Aisha Rahman
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: aisha.rahman@redwood.ai <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Ian Holden <ian.holden@skylabs.com>, SkyLabs SRE <sre@skylabs.com>, contracts@skylabs.com

Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: aurora-lite-v2.3 elevated 5xx/timeouts (root cause & commitments)

Hi Ian / SkyLabs team,

Summary (what happened):
- On 2026-09-12 ~07:50 PT we observed elevated 5xx and timeouts for requests routed to aurora-lite-v2.3. The immediate trigger was a race in the KV-cache eviction code that surfaced only when the quantized kernel path executed under a specific GPU driver + sequence-length distribution.

Root cause:
- A race condition in KV-cache eviction logic for quantized execution caused short-lived kernel crashes on a subset of hosts. When multiple requests with large contexts (>=2k tokens) hit the same host, the crash resulted in request failures (500/504) until autoscaler and fallback routing mitigations engaged.

What we did:
- Disabled quantized kernel for affected pools and diverted 25% of SkyLabs traffic to aurora-stable-2.1 (immediate mitigation).
- Deployed hotfix (aurora-lite v2.3.1) that patches the eviction selector and adds extra validation checks to prevent the race.
- Performed canaries and re-enabled a constrained quantized variant on test hosts before wider rollout.

Impact and timeline:
- Error rate reduced from ~18% to ~2% within 30 minutes of mitigations. Full mitigation and patch rollout completed by 13:00 PT on 2026-09-12.

Customer commitments:
- We will provide a one-time service credit equivalent to 10% of SkyLabs’ September usage bill for the period of elevated errors (Contracts copied).
- We will add a regression test (large-context KV eviction under quantized kernels) to our release gating for aurora variants.
- Engineering will produce a short engineering note that describes the patch and kernel selection logic; we’ll share the note (link above) within 48 hours.

Attachments included: aurora-lite-2.3-kernel-diff.patch (engineering diff), service-bridge-notes-20260912.pdf (timeline), skylabs-logs-09-12.tar.gz (correlated logs).

If you have any remaining production traces you want us to include in the postmortem, please attach them and we’ll fold them into the root-cause doc.

Thanks for your patience and clear reporting — good collaboration on the bridge.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
